source.title: Universal Sharpness Dynamics in Neural Network Training: Fixed Point Analysis, Edge of Stability, and Route to Chaos
source.authors: Dayal Singh Kalra; Tian-Yu He; Maissam Barkeshli

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation affecting the reported findings.
record.tranche_reason: The study analyzes and measures sharpness and training-loss dynamics under different learning rates, initializations, parameterizations, and datasets. Those results bear on V5's edge-of-stability behavior, but the paper does not test the other versions' named outcomes.
record.gate_note: The paper reports that some CIFAR-10 experiments were run until 99% training accuracy, but does not report that accuracy as a result. Results about initialization-dependent sharpness, loss, and edge of stability are recorded where they bear on V5. Cited results from other studies are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study directly tests V5 through gradient-descent loss and sharpness trajectories, UV-model analysis, and initialization and parameterization sweeps. It is not an original source for V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. Add that the UV model cannot reproduce continuing loss descent at EoS, lacks loss catapult at effective width 1, and misses the long-range sharpness correlations seen on realistic datasets.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses gradient descent and MSE loss to analyze sharpness dynamics in a toy linear model and realistic architectures. It does not reproduce the classification-error recipes in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Sharpness and EoS behavior vary with initialization, parameterization, effective width, learning rate, and dataset. Batch size also changes late-time sharpness behavior in the appendix.

fits_no_version.finding: EoS fluctuation structure changes with dataset correlations and activation: period doubling on some synthetic tasks versus dense bands and long-range correlations elsewhere.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The temporal structure of sharpness fluctuations at EoS depends on data covariance and network nonlinearity.

fits_no_version.finding: EoS occurrence correlates positively with test accuracy in the phase diagrams.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: EoS occurrence correlates with generalization performance in the tested sweeps.

record.problems: The main realistic-model measurements use sharpness as the outcome, not training classification error. The CIFAR-10 phase diagrams and several sharpness trajectories are primarily presented in figures, with limited per-condition numeric reporting in text. The authors note that EoS phase boundaries can shift with training duration and that small batches become noise-dominated.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying results omitted. Figure-only phase-diagram cell values were not reconstructed from plots.

untested.parts: No qualifying comparison of convolutional-network training classification error across size, label corruption, or training recipes; the 99% stopping criterion is not such a result.
No matched ReLU teacher-student width sweep measuring spurious local minima or benefits of extra student neurons.
No depth-dependent training-error comparison between plain and residual networks.
No test of signal-preserving initialization effects on learning speed or trainable depth, or orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.
No explicit qualifying result showing divergence from below the initial stability threshold. Recovery and late-time EoS are tested; the record incorrectly lists late-time full-batch EoS as untested.
No batch-normalization versus no-normalization comparison of accuracy gain, learning-rate tolerance, or Fixup training.

missing.what: Catapult recovery above the initial stability limit in large-width NTP UV networks, including reduced curvature after the transient.
Small-variance SP FCNs show the loss and sharpness sequence underlying both catapult recovery and later EoS; no row captures this comparison condition.
At effective width 1, the UV model lacks a useful loss-catapult regime because its catapult threshold is comparable to its maximum trainable learning rate.
NTP FCNs reproduce the initialization-dependent sharpness patterns observed in SP, extending the parameterization comparison.
CNNs and ResNets exhibit EoS across a broader initialization range than FCNs. Full-batch CNN and ResNet sharpness trajectories also show near-threshold late-time behavior.
missing.locator: Appendix F, Figures 21–22; Appendix G.1, Figures 26–27

missing.what: SGD batch size shifts late-time sharpness above or below 2/η depending on initialization and parameterization; ResNet-18 at s = 1 oscillates below 2/η. Record these with their stochastic-training conditions.
missing.locator: Appendices D.2 and F; Figures 11–12, 20 and 22

record.verdict_notes: Only V5 is tested. Dataset-dependent period doubling does not limit a claim that never requires period doubling. Sharpness is a directly relevant measure for V5, but sharpness-only rows cannot establish its accompanying loss behavior.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report training classification error across model sizes, random or corrupted labels, or early stopping.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student sweep over teacher and student widths or spurious-minimum outcomes.
Does not compare plain and shortcut networks' training error as depth changes.
Does not compare initialization methods for learning speed or trainable depth.

Tests sharpness and loss dynamics in UV and realistic models, including initialization and dataset differences. Does not report the full-batch sharpness-threshold behavior over longer times or runs that diverge despite starting below threshold as specified in the version.
Does not compare batch normalization with no normalization for training speed or learning-rate tolerance.

rows.subject: UV model
rows.size_stated: 2-layer linear network; width n and effective width vary by setting
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent on one example with MSE loss; examined the zero-loss fixed line and EoS dynamics.
rows.measure: Stability of zero-loss fixed points and convergence behavior
rows.value: For η < ηc, training converges to stable fixed points on the zero-loss line.
rows.note: The authors state ηc = √neff/∥x∥y for y > 0; this row records the below-threshold condition.
rows.check: Valid comparison condition, but convergence below ηc does not itself establish catapult recovery or sustained EoS. ηc is the threshold destabilizing all zero-loss solutions, not the initial linearized stability limit.

rows.subject: UV model
rows.size_stated: 2-layer linear network; neff = 1 in the bifurcation example
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent on one example with MSE loss as learning rate increases.
rows.measure: Late-time sharpness dynamics and training convergence
rows.baseline: η < ηc: convergence to stable zero-loss fixed points
rows.value: For η > ηc, training converges to the EoS manifold and oscillates; increasing η produces period doubling, followed by divergence at higher rates.
rows.note: The reported threshold is ηc = 0.5 in the stated setting; the bifurcation diagram extends to approximately η ≈ 0.8 before diverging.
rows.check: Sharpness oscillates around 2/η and sufficiently large rates diverge, but the UV model's loss oscillates indefinitely rather than continuing to decrease at EoS. Restrict the EoS condition to convergent trajectories with ηc < η < ηmax; η > ηc alone is insufficient.

source_check.correct: EoS requires ηc < η < ηmax for the initialization; ηc = 0.5 for neff = 1, ||x|| = 1, y = 2. Figure 3(b) extends to approximately η = 0.8 before divergence. η > ηc alone does not ensure bounded EoS dynamics.
source_check.locator_found: Section 5.2, Figure 3, Corollary 5.1; Appendix C.8; Section 7.
source_check.problem: The listed learning-rate condition omits the initialization-dependent upper bound for bounded training.

rows.subject: 4-layer ReLU FCNs, n = 512
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent with MSE loss on 5,000 CIFAR-10 examples; compared parameterization and initialization conditions.
rows.measure: Sharpness trajectory relative to the 2/η edge-of-stability threshold
rows.baseline: SP with σw² = 0.5 and µP with σw² = 2.0 are shown as comparison conditions
rows.value: With SP and σw² = 2.0, the network does not exhibit EoS, even when loss decreases below 10⁻⁵; sharpness mostly decreases, with only a nominal late increase.
rows.note: The text explicitly describes the EoS result and low-loss condition.
rows.check: Correct for the EoS component: large-variance SP networks lack EoS despite loss below 10^-5. This does not show failure of catapult recovery.

rows.subject: 4-layer ReLU FCNs, n = 512
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent with MSE loss on 5,000 CIFAR-10 examples; compared parameterization and initialization conditions.
rows.measure: Sharpness trajectory relative to the 2/η threshold
rows.baseline: SP with σw² = 2.0 does not exhibit EoS in the reported setting
rows.value: Sharpness increases until it reaches 2/η and then oscillates around it; this condition does not experience initial sharpness reduction.
rows.note: This is a comparison condition showing that parameterization changes the reported sharpness dynamics.
rows.check: Correct for progressive sharpening and EoS; absence of initial sharpness reduction at small learning rates does not contradict V5's above-threshold catapult component.

rows.subject: 3-layer ReLU FCNs
rows.operation_detail: Swept weight variance and learning-rate multiplier in a CIFAR-10 EoS phase diagram; plotted test accuracy alongside the sharpness criterion.

conditions.value: weight variance σw² and learning-rate multiplier c = ηλH0

rows.measure: EoS indicator, ηλ̄H/2, and test accuracy
rows.value: The text says the phase diagram validates predictions that small σw² and large c are more likely to exhibit EoS, and reports a positive correlation between observing EoS and improved test accuracy.
rows.note: The paper describes the pattern but does not give numerical values for individual phase-diagram cells in the text.
rows.check: The aggregate mixes conditions exhibiting and lacking EoS; split these where possible. Add the parameterization sweep showing greater EoS prevalence at larger s. Test accuracy is a separate outcome. Figure 4's caption specifies training until 99% accuracy, while Appendix B.3 specifies 10,000 steps; flag this reporting inconsistency.

source_check.locator_found: Section 6.3; Figure 4; Appendix B.3; Appendix F.
source_check.problem: The 10k-step condition is supported by Appendix B.3, but the main Figure 4 caption instead specifies training until 99% training accuracy.

rows.subject: 2-layer linear FCN
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent with MSE loss; compared sharpness fluctuations at EoS on synthetic random data and CIFAR-10.

conditions.value: 5,000 iid random examples with unit output dimension

rows.measure: Sharpness bifurcation and late-time fluctuations at EoS
rows.value: The random-data model exhibits a period-doubling route to chaos and short-period sharpness oscillations; high-frequency modes emerge at EoS.
rows.note: The dataset comparison is central to the paper's account of sharpness behavior at EoS.
rows.check: Supports the sharpness-oscillation component at EoS. Period doubling and its frequency spectrum are additional findings; this row does not establish continuing loss descent.

source_check.locator_found: Section 6.4; Figure 5(a–c); Appendix B.3. The last-1,000-step window applies to the power spectrum.

rows.subject: 2-layer linear FCN
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent with MSE loss; compared sharpness fluctuations at EoS on CIFAR-10 with the random-data condition.
rows.measure: Sharpness bifurcation and late-time fluctuations at EoS
rows.value: The model shows dense sharpness bands rather than a clear period-doubling route to chaos, and long-range correlations in time; high-frequency modes emerge as learning rate increases.
rows.note: The authors distinguish the real-dataset pattern from the synthetic-data route to chaos.
rows.check: Dense bands and long-range correlations occur at EoS. V5 does not require period doubling, so its absence does not make this result partial or limit V5.
